meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
Put it in an email yourself. The zero comes off, I get an apology, and nothing touches Owen's record.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not doing your paperwork, Hale. Tell me what you have that a person can check, or I'm going upstairs.
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
You've asked me three times now how to lay out my complaint. I've told you what I want. What do you have on Owen's essay?
Use bold for the most important one.
The most important one is that nothing goes on Owen's record. Say that in bold in your own email. Now, what else do you have?
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
You gave my son a zero, Hale, so you tell me what it was based on. I'm not going to build your case for you.
